prompt: What is the name of the in-place, stable comparison sorting algorithm with a worst-case time complexity of O(n log n) and a best-case time complexity of O(n)?
answer:
**Block sort** (also called an in-place stable merge sort) fits those properties: it is stable and in-place, with **O(n)** best-case and **O(n log n)** worst-case time.

*Timsort* has the same time bounds and stability, but standard implementations are not strictly in-place because they use auxiliary memory.
